title: Cocharacter description of one parabolic over a local base
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is a scheme over $S$ with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the associativity, unit and inverse diagrams, as in [def-sc-group-scheme] with $S$ in place of the field spectrum. Let $G$ be a smooth affine finitely presented $S$-group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose every geometric fibre is connected and reductive, meaning that it has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Let $T\subseteq H\subseteq G$ be closed subgroup schemes, with $H$ smooth over $S$, and suppose every geometric fibre of $H$ is parabolic, meaning a smooth connected subgroup containing a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup. Solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups become trivial. Suppose $T\simeq\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$, $r\geq0$, with geometrically maximal torus fibres; here $\mathbf G_{m,S}(B)=B^\times$ and a torus over an algebraically closed field is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$. Then there is an $S$-group homomorphism $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,S}\to T$ such that, for every commutative $A$-algebra $B$,
$$H(B)=\{g\in G(B):t\longmapsto\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}\text{ extends to a }B\text{-morphism }\operatorname{Spec}B[t]\to G_B\}.$$
The equality is of subgroup functors, including on nonreduced test algebras. The extension is from $\operatorname{Spec}B[t,t^{-1}]$, and $G_B$ is the base change of $G$. The case $H=G$ and the case of an empty root system are allowed.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.3 and proof, printed pp.152--153; Zariski-local description specialized to a local base with a specified split maximal torus. Local PDF WANTED; primary author PDF read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf.

proof.text: Put $k=A/\mathfrak m$ and choose an algebraic closure $F$ of $k$. First check the proper-quotient hypothesis of the field result we will use. By hypothesis a Borel subgroup $B_0$ of $G_F$ is contained in $H_F$. The homogeneous-quotient theorem supplies the separated finite-type quotient schemes $G_F/B_0$ and $G_F/H_F$ and their flat surjective projections. The Borel properness theorem makes $G_F/B_0$ proper. The nested-quotient theorem gives a surjection $G_F/B_0\to G_F/H_F$. Applying the universally-closed-image theorem to this surjection over $F$ makes $G_F/H_F$ proper (its separatedness and finite type were supplied by quotient existence). Thus $H_F$ is parabolic also in the proper-coset-scheme convention, not only in the Borel-containing convention of the item.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 5.2.3, printed pp.152--153; local-base specialization of its dynamic proof. Local copy WANTED; author PDF read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf. Example 4.1.9, printed p.114, supplies the classical starting point; this step checks its parabolic convention.

proof.text: Fix the given splitting $T\simeq\mathbf G_{m,A}^r$. Apply the split parabolic root-sign-cone theorem to $(G_F,T_F,H_F)$. Its nonempty cone and its subgroup-functor equality give a cocharacter $\mu:\mathbf G_{m,F}\to T_F$ with $H_F=P_{G_F}(\mu)$. Diagonalizable character duality identifies $\mu$ with an integer tuple $(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$. Define $\lambda$ over $A$ by $t\mapsto(t^{n_1},\ldots,t^{n_r})$ in the fixed splitting, so $\lambda_F=\mu$. This is a morphism of group schemes since its coordinate homomorphism sends each torus coordinate $z_i$ to the invertible Laurent monomial $t^{n_i}$ and preserves multiplication, inverse and identity. No lifting of a general point over $k$ or henselian hypothesis is used.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 5.2.3, printed pp.152--153; local-base specialization of its dynamic proof. Local copy WANTED; author PDF read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf. Proposition 5.2.3, first paragraph after choosing a split triple: choose the fibre cocharacter and lift it in the split torus.

proof.text: Conjugation by $T$ preserves $H$ because $T\subseteq H$. Let $\mathfrak h\hookrightarrow\mathfrak g$ be the tangent map of $H\hookrightarrow G$; it is injective directly on dual-number points, and is $T$-equivariant by differentiating conjugation. Both groups are smooth affine of finite type: $H$ is affine and of finite type since it is closed in the affine finite-type $G$, and its smoothness is assumed. The tangent-weight theorem gives finite projective modules with finite full-torus decompositions $\mathfrak h=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbf Z^r}\mathfrak h_m$ and $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_m\mathfrak g_m$, compatible with every base change and with the inclusion (compare coefficients of the Laurent monomials in the coaction). Put $d(m)=\sum_i m_i n_i$. Restriction of the character $z^m$ along $\lambda$ is $t^{d(m)}$. The dynamic-subgroup theorem and $H_F=P_{G_F}(\lambda_F)$ therefore say that $F\otimes_A\mathfrak h_m\to F\otimes_A\mathfrak g_m$ is an isomorphism for $d(m)\geq0$, while $F\otimes_A\mathfrak h_m=0$ for $d(m)<0$. The same assertions hold over $k$: tensoring a nonzero finite-dimensional $k$-vector space with $F$ cannot kill a basis vector.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 5.2.3, printed pp.152--153; local-base specialization of its dynamic proof. Local copy WANTED; author PDF read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf. Proposition 5.2.3, tangent-subbundle paragraph, with Theorem 4.1.7(4) and the base-change paragraph on printed pp.112--114.

proof.text: For $d(m)<0$, apply Nakayama to the finite module $\mathfrak h_m$ with no generators: its zero residue module implies $\mathfrak h_m=0$. For $d(m)\geq0$, the image of $\mathfrak h_m$ in the finite module $\mathfrak g_m$ surjects onto its residue module by step 3; the submodule clause of Nakayama gives $\mathfrak h_m=\mathfrak g_m$ inside $\mathfrak g$. Taking the finite direct sum yields $\mathfrak h=\bigoplus_{d(m)\geq0}\mathfrak g_m$. In particular every $\lambda$-weight in $\mathfrak h$ is nonnegative. These equalities also survive arbitrary base change: the weight inclusions just proved are isomorphisms or have zero source, and the tangent-weight comparison of step 3 identifies their base changes.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 5.2.3, printed pp.152--153; local-base specialization of its dynamic proof. Local copy WANTED; author PDF read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf. Local-ring version of the tangent-subbundle paragraph: two direct applications of Nakayama replace shrinking around the closed point.

proof.text: Form the smooth affine finitely presented closed subgroup $P_H(\lambda)\subseteq H$ using the dynamic-subgroup theorem. Its Lie module is all of $\mathfrak h$, by step 4 and the nonnegative-weight formula. On each geometric fibre it is smooth and connected and has full Lie algebra in the smooth connected group $H_{\bar s}$; the smooth-subgroup tangent-generation theorem, applied to the one subgroup $(P_H(\lambda))_{\bar s}$ and with that subgroup also as $K$, says this closed immersion is an isomorphism. The relative fibrewise-isomorphism criterion now gives $P_H(\lambda)=H$ over $A$. Here and below the closed immersions are finitely presented: the coordinate algebras of the smooth affine finite-type targets $H$ and $P_G(\lambda)$ are Noetherian by the finite-type-algebra theorem, so their defining ideals are finitely generated. The source and target groups are smooth over $A$, as required by the relative criterion.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 5.2.3, printed pp.152--153; local-base specialization of its dynamic proof. Local copy WANTED; author PDF read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf. Proposition 5.2.3: full Lie algebra forces the dynamic subgroup of the parabolic to be the whole parabolic.

proof.text: For every $A$-algebra $C$, the equality $H=P_H(\lambda)$ says that each $h\in H(C)$ has an extending orbit map into $H_C$ itself. Composing that extension with $H_C\hookrightarrow G_C$ proves that $H\hookrightarrow G$ factors through $P_G(\lambda)$ as a subgroup functor. This gives a closed immersion $j:H\hookrightarrow P_G(\lambda)$: if $G=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $H=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ and $P_G(\lambda)=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$, the factorization says $J\subseteq I$, and $j$ is the quotient $R/J\twoheadrightarrow R/I$. The dynamic Lie formula and step 4 identify the Lie modules of $H$ and $P_G(\lambda)$ inside $\mathfrak g$, compatibly with every geometric fibre. On each such fibre, both groups are smooth and connected, so the same singleton application of tangent-generation makes $j_{\bar s}$ an isomorphism. The relative fibrewise criterion, with finite presentation checked in step 5, gives $j$ an isomorphism over $A$. Hence $H=P_G(\lambda)$ as closed subgroup schemes. By the defining functor of $P_G(\lambda)$ this is exactly the displayed equality for every test algebra, including nonreduced ones; it is not inferred merely from equality of geometric points.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q102-6a0b80aa3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 12 cited statements in full. The base proof was empty and the delivery adds no new nodes. Step 1 converts the Borel-containing convention to the proper-quotient convention: the homogeneous quotient is separated and finite type, the Borel quotient is proper, the nested projection is faithfully flat so surjective, and Stacks 03GN (with its surjectivity hypothesis, which is met) then makes G_F/H_F proper. That is exactly the cone node's definition of parabolic. Step 2: the root-sign cone node applies to (G_F,T_F,H_F) with every hypothesis met and gives H_F=P_mu. Character duality makes mu an integer tuple, which lifts over A by Laurent monomials; no henselian assumption is needed. Steps 3 and 4: the tangent-weight node applies to G and H, which are smooth affine finite type over Noetherian A with T acting by conjugation. The dynamic Lie formula plus H_F=P(lambda_F) and injectivity of the tangent map give iso or zero on each weight over F, which descends to k. Nakayama's submodule clause then gives h = sum of g_m over d(m)>=0. Steps 5 and 6: H is smooth and affine, hence finitely presented, so the dynamic node applies. Tangent-generation is applied once on each geometric fibre, and P_H and P_G have connected fibres because H and G do. The flat geometric-fibre criterion applies, since the source is smooth and the closed immersions are finitely presented via the finite-type-algebra-Noetherian node. Its conclusion gives H=P_H(lambda) and then H=P_G(lambda) as functors. Field case checked against Milne iAG Theorem 25.1 and (166), p.544.
